The **contradictions arise from secondary sources** (e.g., diplomatic statements, editorials) rather than primary legal texts. 3. The **2023/2024 "amendments"** are likely inferred from political rhetoric (e.g., Trump administration statements) rather than formal treaties. **Uncertainty:** - The exact 1951 agreement may exist in **restricted archives** (e.g., U.S. State Department, Danish Foreign Ministry) not indexed by public-web-read. - The "alleged expansions" could be **misinterpreted diplomatic gestures** (e.g., expanded military access) rather than formal treaty changes. --- **Concrete Test:** **Action:** Use the approved public-search capability to query **official government repositories** (e.g., [U.S. National Archives](https://www.archives.gov/), [Danish Ministry of Foreign Affairs](https://um.dk/)) for the **full text of the 1951 Defense Agreement** and any **2023/2024 amendments**, specifying: - Keywords: *"1951 Defense Agreement Greenland," "Annex to 1951 Defense Agreement," "2023/2024 Greenland Defense Update," "Denmark-U.S. Mutual Defense Treaty."* - File types: PDF, scanned documents, or official gazettes. - Date ranges: 1951 (original) and 2023–2024 (alleged updates). **Expected Outcome:** - If the text is retrievable, it will resolve contradictions by providing **direct legal language** for comparison. - If unretrievable, it confirms the **gap in public records** and justifies querying **untrusted outside leads** (e.g., diplomatic cables via FOIA requests) or the **Archive** for reviewed evidence.
